rules.cwe_name: Data Processing Errors
rules.description: Legacy category for incorrect handling or transformation of structured data.

rules.cwe_name: Dead Code
rules.description: Duplicate key in dict literal. All but the last will be lost.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
rules.description: Matching HTML tags using regular expressions is hard to do right, and can easily lead to security issues.

rules.cwe_name: Function Call With Incorrect Number of Arguments
rules.description: A string formatting operation, such as '"%s: %s, %s" % (a,b)', where the number of conversion specifiers in the format string differs from the number of values to be formatted will raise a TypeError.

rules.cwe_name: Generation of Predictable Numbers or Identifiers
rules.description: Tokens used for sensitive tasks, such as, password recovery, and email confirmation, should not use predictable values.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Control of Document Type Definition
rules.description: Parsing user input as an XML document with external entity expansion is vulnerable to XXE attacks.

rules.cwe_name: Function Call With Incorrectly Specified Argument Value
rules.description: Calling super with something other than the enclosing class may cause incorrect object initialization.

rules.cwe_name: Active Debug Code
rules.description: Running a Flask app in debug mode may allow an attacker to run arbitrary code through the Werkzeug debugger.

rules.cwe_name: Security Issue (CWE-730)
rules.description: User input should not be used in regular expressions without first being escaped, otherwise a malicious user may be able to inject an expression that could require exponential time on certain inputs.

rules.cwe_name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
